To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a natural logic of knowledge, branching time and common knowledge for reasoning about distributed system, and that we have shown that satisfiability for this logic remains in PSPACE.

the propositional dynamic logic with converse already suffices for the interpretation of the propositional logic of common knowledge and branching time, and that the propositional logic with common knowledge and branching is EMPTIME-complete.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the formalization of the logic of knowledge, which is a natural propositional logic with knowledge and common knowledge modalities and branching time appropriate to reasoning about distributed systems.
the following questions: What are the basic concepts and properties of knowledge and knowledge-based systems that can be formalised?
the following questions: What are the properties of a natural logic of knowledge appropriate for reasoning about the behavior of distributed systems?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
The logic of knowledge is not a logic in the sense of a set of inference rules, but a logic in the mathematical sense of a set-theoretic model of a formal language.
the logic of knowledge and branching time presented in this dissertation provides a framework for reasoning about the properties of distributed protocols.

the logic of knowledge, in the form we have described it, is a natural and useful tool for reasoning about distributed computing, and that the logic of common knowledge is not a natural or useful extension of the logic of knowledge in this context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that PDLC is a natural logic for reasoning about knowledge in branching time.
we are able to prove that satisfiability of propositional logic of temporal and epistemic operators is in the class of EMPTIME, which means it is in PSPACE.

we show that PDLC already provides a natural semantics for a certain logic of knowledge, and that the logic is expressive enough to be able to express all the properties of interest in distributed systems, and yet not too expressive so that it does not make the complexity of satisfiability explode.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the logic of knowledge and common knowl-edge can be interpreted in a natural way in PDLC.
the logic of knowledge is not a separate and distinct logic.

PDLC already provides a very expressive and natural logic of knowledge, branching time, and converse for reasoning about distributed system protocols, and that it can be used to reason about knowledge and branching time without the need for a special-purpose modal logic of knowledge and branching time.
